key_insight: A Fourier neural operator surrogate learns to correct low-cost Boussinesq natural-convection simulations toward compressible-flow accuracy with a single model evaluation per case.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to faster, higher-fidelity thermal-flow prediction for CFD workflows where repeated natural convection solves are needed.
method: Generate paired training data from matched Boussinesq and compressible simulations.
Train Fourier neural operators on 2D and 3D flow fields to map cheap predictions to high-fidelity corrections.
Implement both solvers with parallel implicit monolithic mixed FEM in FEniCSx and validate against COMSOL and benchmark problems.
evidence_signal: Using compressible-flow solutions as references, the surrogate achieved SSIM close to 1 across variables and test distributions, with MSE reductions from one to nearly three orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of paired simulation data, and generalization beyond the tested natural-convection regimes remains to be verified.
paper_title: A Neural Surrogate Approach for Simulating Natural Convection Problems
